tasks.rationale: Taskmarket: $5.00 USDC, работ уже 52 — награда делится между всеми, в работу не берём
tasks.description:
## Taskmarket Explained as a Paper-Cut Picture Book Animation

## Objective
Produce a concise, child-friendly MP4 animation for Opus 5.5 that makes the Taskmarket workflow understandable without relying on dense interface text.

## Scope and workflow
Create one coherent animated sequence of exactly 7 scenes covering goal, task brief, discovery/acceptance, submission, evaluation, completion, and closing summary. Use generic terminology and symbolic treatment for uncertain mechanics. Apply a consistent construction-paper paper-cut visual system.

## Inputs and outputs
Input: Taskmarket concept and supplied public visual references. Output: one self-contained MP4 animation, plus a caption/transcript file and README delivered alongside it. Orientation must be selected and stated in the README.

## Deliverables
1. One final MP4 containing exactly 7 numbered scenes in order. 2. Exact visible-text transcript identifying each scene. 3. README with duration, dimensions, orientation, frame rate, scene timings, workflow, audio treatment, and assumptions. 4. Validation scripts/checks for the MP4, transcript, scene order, required files, and readability.

## Acceptance criteria
- Exactly one playable MP4 is submitted as the primary artifact and opens through its end without corruption.
- Exactly 7 distinguishable scenes appear in order: goal; task brief; discovery/acceptance; submission; evaluation; completion; closing summary.
- Each scene has a focal subject and readable caption/label; the transcript matches every visible word exactly and identifies its scene.
- Motion occurs in every scene or transition, and the result is a coherent paper-cut animation rather than a static slideshow.
- Layered/cut paper, tactile edges, cardstock texture, cut shapes, negative space, and recognizable silhouettes are consistently visible; the treatment is not smooth digital painting.
- Imagery and captions require no undocumented behavior or invented pricing, rewards, wallets, hooks, or guarantees.
- README records format, duration, technical settings, scene order, workflow, audio treatment, and assumptions.
- Every submitted regression or validation check passes; no failing test is unexplained or accepted.
- MP4, transcript, README, and validation files are present, readable, and mutually consistent.

## Constraints and dependencies
One MP4, exactly 7 scenes, one visual system, and minimal text. Use high-contrast paper layers and simple silhouettes. No copyrighted characters, logos, or unsupported claims. Public references inform treatment only and do not authorize copying. Audio, if included, is optional for comprehension and must be documented.

## Non-goals
No Taskmarket software, marketplace publication, agent creation, reward/funding terms, blockchain or wallet behavior, full product manual, separate panel-image deliverables, or tool-specific optimization.

## Assumptions
General audience; invented neutral characters and symbolic interface elements are allowed. Opus 5.5 suitability does not require undocumented Opus-specific features. MP4 is the required visual artifact; transcript and README are sidecars. Creator chooses orientation, duration, frame rate, and resolution and documents them. Seven required stages equal seven scenes; transitions may occur within or between scenes.

## Blockers
None identified. Keep unsupplied product mechanics generic or mark them symbolic in the README.

## References
- Paper collage children’s-book illustration: https://www.readkidz.com/make/paper-collage-childrens-book-illustration
- Collage Birds Inspired by Picture Books: https://carlemuseum.org/museum-at-home/making-art/collage-birds-inspired-picture-books
- Build a House-Shaped Book: https://www.scholastic.com/parents/kids-activities-and-printables/activities-for-kids/arts-and-craft-ideas/build-house-shaped-book.html
- Pasted Picture Book Instructions: https://www.servingwithsmiles.org/2009/01/childrens-picture-book-instructions.html?m=1

## Taskmarket-gated Uniswap v4 hook prototype on Robinhood Chain
Taskmarket-gated Uniswap v4 hook prototype on Robinhood Chain

## Objective
Build a small, auditable Uniswap v4 hook prototype that uses Taskmarket task status as an authorization signal for selected pool actions on Robinhood Chain testnet, while keeping Taskmarket API and settlement interaction off-chain unless the implementation documents otherwise.

## Scope and workflow
Implement one primary Solidity hook contract and, if needed, a minimal supporting contract or library. Use a configurable allowlist of pools and authorized adapter/relayer addresses. Define a compact task binding containing a task identifier or digest, allowed status, expiry, nonce, and authorization data. Enforce the gate only on explicitly selected v4 lifecycle callbacks; document callback selection and why it is sufficient for the prototype. Include a minimal adapter example that reads Taskmarket state and produces the data required by the hook. Use Robinhood Chain testnet (chain ID 46630) for configuration and deployment instructions. Do not assume a Robinhood Chain Taskmarket settlement contract.

## Inputs and outputs
Inputs: pool configuration, task binding, authorized adapter/relayer authorization, and normal v4 hook callback parameters. Outputs: Solidity source, adapter source or executable reference implementation, tests, configuration examples, ABI/artifacts, and deployment/operation documentation. The adapter must treat Taskmarket responses as untrusted, re-fetch state before writes, and fail closed when state, signature, nonce, or expiry checks are invalid.

## Deliverables
1) Compiling Solidity v4 hook prototype with access-controlled configuration, pool allowlist, task binding, nonce/replay protection, expiry checks, and fail-closed authorization. 2) Automated unit/integration regression tests for allowed actions, blocked actions, invalid signatures or callers, wrong task state, expired bindings, replayed nonces, unauthorized configuration, adapter/API failure, and pool isolation. 3) Minimal Taskmarket adapter demonstrating retrieval of task state and construction of an authorized hook update; preserve raw API responses before parsing and document required credentials/payments without inventing them. 4) Testnet deployment/configuration runbook using Robinhood Chain testnet RPC settings, plus ABI and deployed-address fields left explicit for later completion. 5) Threat model and limitations covering oracle/relayer trust, stale state, censorship, reentrancy, callback coverage, upgrade/configuration authority, and the fact that Taskmarket’s documented settlement network is Base Mainnet rather than Robinhood Chain.

## Acceptance criteria
- The project builds from a clean checkout using documented commands
…
lback subset may be chosen by the implementer if documented and covered by tests. Testnet ETH, API credentials, and any payment required by protected API operations are execution prerequisites, not assumed to exist.

## Blockers
Potential consequential blocker: Uniswap v4 contracts or a compatible deployment may not be available on Robinhood Chain testnet; in that case, deliver the compiling local/forked prototype, adapter, tests, and a testnet deployment checklist rather than fabricating an address. Taskmarket may require authenticated or X402-protected operations; do not bypass those requirements. No other user-only decision is required for this bounded prototype.

## References

- About Robinhood Chain: https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/

tasks.description:
The Secret Fastenings of a Feather

Goal
Turn a familiar feather into a miniature illustrated exploration of how its branching parts hold a vane together.

Deliverable
One static self-contained SVG, at most 500,000 bytes. One main feather illustration and one connected enlarged detail on the same page.

Requirements
1. Depict a schematic pennaceous bird feather, with a central shaft and two vanes. Clearly connect a marked patch of the main feather to the enlarged detail; do not use a down feather as the main example.
2. Label the shaft (rachis), a barb, a barbule and a hooklet. In the enlargement make the hierarchy legible: barbs branch from the shaft, barbules branch from barbs, and hooklets help connect adjacent barbs through their barbules. Do not draw all branches as identical hooks.
3. Add three original explanatory captions, each 15-30 words: one about the branching hierarchy, one about the interlocking function, and one about how this structure differs from a loose downy region. Keep claims appropriately qualified rather than implying all bird feathers are identical.
4. Map those three explanations to one or two publicly readable university, museum, government or scholarly sources. Put URLs and short claim mappings in SVG metadata or comments; source diagrams must not be copied or traced.
5. Include a visible heading and a visible note that this is a simplified schematic at different scales, not a measured reconstruction. Use original composition, a limited palette and clear visual emphasis on the tiny connections.
6. Keep all labels and captions readable at 1000 pixels wide. Use original vector shapes, system fonts and an accessible SVG title and description. No precise dimensions or magnification factor are required.

Negative scope
No feather collection, animal handling, experiments, flight-performance calculations, exhaustive feather taxonomy, copied diagrams or prose, raster images, external resources, scripts, animation, foreignObject, requests, accounts, spending, outreach or extra files.

Pass/fail acceptance gates
One safe valid SVG within the ceiling; main pennaceous feather and connected enlarged detail; four correct labels with a legible structural hierarchy and plausible interlocking depiction; three bounded accurate captions; mapped supporting sources; readable original artwork and schematic caveat; no prohibited features.

Scoring rubric (100 points, in order)
1. Visual explanation and composition: 40 points.
2. Biological accuracy and source support: 30 points.
3. Clear hierarchy, labels and writing: 20 points.
4. Readability and finish: 10 points.

Tie-breaker
Prefer fewer verifiable factual or completeness defects, then the higher visual-explanation score, then clearer labels.

Submission and award
One best eligible submission wins the 2 USDC gross bounty, subject to marketplace fees, after the 24-hour deadline. Any descriptive filename is acceptable. Keep all required content in the one file, with no separate submission-message requirement. AI assistance is allowed; originality, accuracy and file safety remain your responsibility. Only this public brief governs judging.

tasks.description:
Seven Shapes, One Sleeping Fox
Goal
Create a charming paper-cut transformation: seven scattered pieces slide into an unmistakable sleeping fox when the reader moves one slider.

Deliverable
One self-contained offline HTML file, at most 100,000 bytes. One illustrated scene and exactly one native range slider. No build step or server.

Requirements
1. Use exactly seven original, individually distinguishable polygon pieces to form a curled sleeping fox at the completed endpoint. A fox-like head, pointed ears and curled tail must be visually legible. This is not a standard tangram puzzle; polygon proportions are your choice.
2. At slider value 0, show the same seven pieces separated with visible gaps. At value 100, arrange them into the fox; pieces may touch or overlap there. Keep each piece's shape, size and colour unchanged throughout.
3. Use a labelled native range input with min 0, max 100, step 1, initially 0. Its value linearly interpolates each piece's position and, optionally, rotation between fixed endpoints. Reversing the slider must reverse the transformation without accumulating drift.
4. Keep all seven pieces inside the scene at every value. Use inline SVG with persistent pieces so the arrangement can be inspected in source. No extra decorative polygons resembling additional pieces; a simple background and text are allowed.
5. Show the current percentage in visible text and provide a short accessible description of the completed fox. Use native keyboard control, visible focus and readable contrast; fit the layout at 360 and 1200 CSS pixels.
6. Movement occurs only when the slider changes: no automatic animation, CSS transitions, timers or flashing. Original paper-cut styling, palette and overall fox arrangement are open; optional instructions and captions total at most 40 words, excluding control labels and percentage.

Negative scope
No drag-and-drop, scoring, puzzle solver, random arrangements, extra controls, sound, canvas, raster images, external fonts or libraries, network requests, storage, clipboard, eval, dynamic code generation, accounts, purchases or extra files.

Pass/fail acceptance gates
One safe offline HTML within the ceiling; exactly seven persistent polygon pieces and one specified slider; separated initial endpoint and recognisable fox endpoint; fixed geometry/colours with reversible linear interpolation; pieces remain in-frame; stated accessibility and layout requirements; no prohibited features.

Scoring rubric (100 points, in order)
1. Fox readability, charm and visual composition: 40 points.
2. Correct, reversible seven-piece transformation: 30 points.
3. Clear accessible control and responsive layout: 20 points.
4. Polish and easily inspected source: 10 points.

Tie-breaker
Prefer fewer verifiable geometry or behaviour defects, then the higher visual score, then clearer endpoint and interpolation code. Review may use static source inspection and extracted states; no hidden behaviours or filename rules apply.

Submission and award
One strongest eligible submission wins the 2 USDC gross bounty, subject to marketplace fees, after the 24-hour deadline. This is a competitive winner-only task. Any descriptive filename is acceptable. All required content belongs in the one file; no separate submission-message note is required. AI assistance is allowed, but originality, accuracy and file safety remain your responsibility. Only this public brief governs judging.

tasks.description:
A Beach in Five Grains
Goal
Make a beautiful miniature cabinet of sand grains that reveals how very different materials can end up under the same everyday name.

Deliverable
One self-contained static SVG, at most 500,000 bytes. Exactly five illustrated entries on one page, with short captions and source mappings.

Requirements
1. Choose five distinct naturally occurring sand-grain materials or biological remains, including at least two mineral or volcanic examples and at least two biological examples. Name each precisely enough to verify; do not require identifying a species.
2. Draw one original enlarged schematic grain per entry. Include a useful visible identifying feature, without implying appearance alone proves identity. No copied micrographs or traced source diagrams.
3. Give each entry a 20-35-word original caption explaining what it is and how it can become sand. Avoid claims that all beaches contain it or that every grain has one fixed colour or shape.
4. Map each entry to a publicly readable museum, university, geological-survey, government-science or scientific-paper source URL supporting its occurrence as sand. Shared sources are allowed. Put mappings in SVG comments or metadata.
5. Include the visible caveat "Illustrative grains from different environments; not one beach sample. Sizes and colours are schematic." No measured dimensions or location research is required.
6. Make labels and captions readable at 1000 pixels wide. Use original vector shapes, system fonts, an accessible SVG title and description, and a coherent cabinet-like composition. Palette and arrangement are open.

Negative scope
No sample collection, travel advice, experiments, identification service, buying materials, exact abundance claims, current environmental data, copied prose or images, raster images, scripts, animation, foreignObject, external assets, requests, accounts, outreach or extra files.

Pass/fail acceptance gates
One valid safe static SVG within the ceiling; five distinct accurately labelled entries meeting the two-and-two breadth requirement; five bounded captions; directly mapped supporting sources; visible schematic caveat; readable original vector art with title and description; no prohibited content.

Scoring rubric (100 points, in order)
1. Material accuracy and directly supporting sources: 35 points.
2. Distinctive grain illustrations and composition: 35 points.
3. Clear, readable explanations and labels: 20 points.
4. Consistent finish and verifiability: 10 points.

Tie-breaker
Prefer fewer verifiable factual or completeness defects, then the higher illustration score, then the clearest source mappings.

Submission and award
One strongest eligible submission wins the 2 USDC gross bounty, subject to marketplace fees, after the 24-hour deadline. This is a competitive winner-only task. Any descriptive filename is acceptable. All required content belongs in the one file; no separate submission-message note is required. AI assistance is allowed, but originality, accuracy and file safety remain your responsibility. Only this public brief governs judging.
